#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Fetch all RippleState trust lines from a given XRP Ledger ledger
and return only those where LowLimit.issuer == HighLimit.issuer.

Notes

- Handles both plain and 'FinalFields' wrapped entries.
- Streams results to a JSONL file to avoid high memory usage.

      --server https://s1.ripple.com:51234 \
      --ledger-hash 842B57C1CC0613299A686D3E9F310EC0422C84D3911E5056389AA7E5808A93C8 \
      --out matches.js

reviewCommentsList.author: drlongle
reviewCommentsList.body:
If the first call to `removeTrustLineToSelf` fails, the second call to `removeTrustLineToSelf` will not be executed. This is due to [short-circuit evaluation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Short-circuit_evaluation).

I am not sure if this is intended but just want to point it out.

reviewCommentsList.author: drlongle
reviewCommentsList.body: I would drop `!view().rules().enabled(fixTrustLinesToSelf)` because I don't know if all trust lines to self have been deleted. I feel that this is less defensive as it could be.

reviewCommentsList.author: intelliot
reviewCommentsList.body: - Can't drop that because there are currently two trustlines to self. Without the check, servers with and without this PR would behave differently.

reviewCommentsList.author: drlongle
reviewCommentsList.body:
The code says that if `fixTrustLinesToSelf` is disabled and `account_ == uDstAccountID`, we can delete a trustline. Once `fixTrustLinesToSelf` is enabled, no other self-issued trustlines will be deleted because the first operand of the `&&` operator will be false.

This is fine as long as we know that there are **only** two self-issued trustlines on the ledger.

reviewCommentsList.author: a-noni-mousse
reviewCommentsList.body: I did on purpose so if deletion fails amendment activation fails and does a roll back, but deletion would not fail.
